newsitem.title: USA: MCI quietly cuts MCI One charges for some.
newsitem.headline: MCI quietly cuts MCI One charges for some.

text.p: MCI Communications Corp on Thursday said it cut long distance charges 20 percent and used six-second billing for residential and small business users on the MCI One plan who spent more than $25 per month.

MCI One customers who signed up since January 1 and who meet the minimum bill requirement have been offered a flat $0.12 per minute rate instead of the old $0.15 rate, MCI said, confirming a report in USA Today.
These users also get billed in units of six seconds instead of a minimum minute, which can save a great deal for those who make short calls or leave a lot of voicemail.

Existing MCI One customers who request the new rate and billing structure will get it, if their monthly bills have exceeded $25, but MCI will not automatically move all qualifying MCI One customers, a spokesman said.
The new charges do not affect large business customers who use MCI One.

The rate compares with AT&T Corp's flat One Rate 15 cents plan, and a $0.14 flat rate for GTE Corp. Other carriers have lower rates for off-peak calls, like Sprint Corp with its $0.10 a minute offering.
MCI has not advertised the new rates and declined to make a senior executive available to explain the strategy.
However, analysts say that it conforms to industry trends to segment the market as much as possible.

This means offering highly competitive rates for those customers who are very price sensitive and who may otherwise leave for competitors, and nudging up basic rates for users not on calling plans, or who seem not to be price sensitive.
MCI increased its basic long distance rates by 4.9 percent in November. MCI is in the process of merging with British Telecommunications Plc.
MCI earlier this month said it cut its rates to Britain to $0.12 from $0.29, which will apply to calling card calls too.
An MCI spokesman on Thursday said that the $0.89 surcharge on international calling card calls had been scrapped from the start of this year. (( Nick Louth, New York Newsroom 212 859 1712))
